redundancies.title: PAYROLL_DETAILS.ELEMENT_TYPE duplicates PAY_ELEMENTS.ELEMENT_TYPE
redundancies.description: PAYROLL_DETAILS stores ELEMENT_TYPE as a direct copy of PAY_ELEMENTS.ELEMENT_TYPE at the time of payroll calculation. This was done for 'query performance' (comment in schema). However, if a PAY_ELEMENT's type is ever changed, historical PAYROLL_DETAILS rows will not reflect the change — creating a silent divergence.
redundancies.divergence_risk: HIGH — no trigger or constraint keeps these in sync
redundancies.recommendation: For most queries, join PAY_ELEMENTS to get ELEMENT_TYPE. Remove the denormalized column unless payroll historical snapshot semantics are explicitly required (in which case, document the intent clearly).

redundancies.title: VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY available balance formula differs from LEAVE_BALANCES virtual column
redundancies.primary_source: LEAVE_BALANCES.AVAILABLE (virtual column): OPENING_BALANCE + ACCRUED - USED + ADJUSTMENT - PENDING
redundancies.description: The view omits the subtraction of PENDING days from the available balance formula. Any report or Oracle Form that uses VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY will overstate available leave for employees who have pending (submitted but not yet approved) leave requests. The authoritative formula is in the virtual column.
redundancies.divergence_risk: ACTIVE BUG — employees can submit overlapping leave requests
redundancies.recommendation: Fix VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY to match the virtual column: change to OPENING_BALANCE + ACCRUED - USED + ADJUSTMENT - PENDING.

redundancies.title: TRG_EMP_BEFORE_UPDATE uses column names that do not match EMPLOYEE_HISTORY DDL
redundancies.primary_source: EMPLOYEE_HISTORY DDL columns: HIST_ID, EFFECTIVE_DATE, OLD_DEPT_ID, NEW_DEPT_ID, OLD_JOB_ID, NEW_JOB_ID, OLD_SALARY, NEW_SALARY
redundancies.redundant_copy: TRG_EMP_BEFORE_UPDATE INSERT columns: HISTORY_ID, CHANGE_DATE, OLD_VALUE, NEW_VALUE
redundancies.description: The trigger attempts to insert into EMPLOYEE_HISTORY using column names that do not match the DDL. This will raise ORA-00904 (invalid identifier) at runtime, meaning all STATUS_CHANGE, DEPARTMENT_CHANGE, and JOB_CHANGE history records are silently failing to insert. The trigger may also be catching the exception internally and swallowing it.
redundancies.divergence_risk: CRITICAL — employee change history is likely missing or corrupt
redundancies.recommendation: Determine which version is authoritative (DDL or trigger). If DDL is correct: (1) rewrite the trigger INSERT to use HIST_ID, EFFECTIVE_DATE, OLD_DEPT_ID, etc.; (2) replace 'DEPARTMENT_CHANGE' with 'TRANSFER' and 'JOB_CHANGE' with 'PROMOTION'/'DEMOTION' to comply with CHK_CHANGE_TYPE — both values are absent from the actual constraint (`HIRE, TRANSFER, PROMOTION, DEMOTION, SALARY_CHANGE, TERMINATION, REHIRE, LEAVE_START, LEAVE_END, STATUS_CHANGE`). Note: a prior review pass suggested 'DEPT_CHANGE' as the fix, but 'DEPT_CHANGE' does NOT appear in the real constraint. CORRECTED by DA Agent 2 (pass 2).

redundancies.title: SSN validation rules differ between client (Oracle Forms) and server (PKG_COMMON)
redundancies.primary_source: HRMS_VALIDATION_LIB.pll validate_ssn: checks all-zero segments (000-xx-xxxx, xxx-00-xxxx, xxx-xx-0000)
redundancies.redundant_copy: PKG_COMMON.is_valid_ssn: does NOT check all-zero segments
redundancies.description: A user entering SSN 000-12-3456 via the Oracle Forms client will receive a validation error (client rejects it). If the same SSN is submitted via a direct package call or a future API, it passes server-side validation and gets stored. This creates a maintenance trap: anyone bypassing the form can store SSNs that the form would reject.
redundancies.divergence_risk: MEDIUM — data quality gap if server-side procedures are called directly
redundancies.recommendation: Add all-zero segment checks to PKG_COMMON.is_valid_ssn to match client-side rules.

redundancies.title: Email validation rejects subdomains in client but not server
redundancies.description: Client-side email regex does not allow subdomains. Server-side validation does. Employees with legitimate subdomain emails cannot enter them via the form but they can be stored if inserted directly.
redundancies.divergence_risk: LOW — functional gap for edge case employees with subdomain email
redundancies.recommendation: Update client-side validation to allow subdomains per RFC 5322.

redundancies.title: Two business-day calculation functions with different holiday behavior
redundancies.description: Two functions calculate the number of business days between two dates, but they use different rules. The PKG_LEAVE version excludes public holidays; the PKG_COMMON version does not. Callers that use the PKG_COMMON version for leave-related calculations will overcount working days.
redundancies.divergence_risk: MEDIUM — PKG_REPORTING may use the non-holiday-aware version for SLA calculations
redundancies.recommendation: Consolidate into one function. Add a p_include_holidays parameter or always use PKG_LEAVE.calculate_business_days as the standard.

redundancies.title: Tax brackets hard-coded in PKG_PAYROLL despite TAX_BRACKETS table existing
redundancies.primary_source: TAX_BRACKETS table: designed to store annual tax brackets by year and filing status
redundancies.redundant_copy: PKG_PAYROLL private constants: 2024 federal brackets, standard deductions, SS wage base
redundancies.description: The TAX_BRACKETS table exists and contains the structure for dynamic bracket lookup, but PKG_PAYROLL ignores it entirely and uses hard-coded 2024 values. This means: (1) the table and its seed data are dead weight; (2) 2025 tax calculations will be incorrect until the package is recompiled; (3) the TAX_BRACKETS table's content cannot be validated against what the system actually uses.
redundancies.recommendation: Remove hard-coded constants from PKG_PAYROLL. Implement lookup from TAX_BRACKETS by p_tax_year. This unblocks annual tax updates without code deployment.

redundancies.title: SEQ_EMP_NUMBER exists but is never used
redundancies.description: SEQ_EMP_NUMBER was likely intended as the primary mechanism for generating EMP_NUMBER values. Instead, PKG_EMPLOYEE uses a MAX()+1 approach, leaving the sequence as an unused object. The sequence starts at 1000, which may conflict with the format EMP-NNNNNN if SEQ_EMP_NUMBER were ever activated.
redundancies.divergence_risk: LOW — the unused sequence wastes no data but is a maintenance confusion
redundancies.recommendation: Retire SEQ_EMP_NUMBER or switch PKG_EMPLOYEE to use it (after aligning starting value with current MAX(EMP_NUMBER)).

redundancies.title: VW_PAYROLL_LATEST.latest_run identified by MAX(RUN_ID) not MAX(RUN_DATE)
redundancies.primary_source: PAYROLL_RUNS.RUN_DATE: the actual date of the run
redundancies.redundant_copy: VW_PAYROLL_LATEST: uses MAX(RUN_ID) as proxy for latest
redundancies.description: The view assumes RUN_ID is a monotonically increasing proxy for recency. This breaks for supplemental or bonus runs inserted after a later regular run — the supplemental run would have a lower RUN_ID than the next regular run, causing the view to misidentify the 'latest' run for a period.
redundancies.divergence_risk: MEDIUM — payroll summary reports could show wrong run for a given period
redundancies.recommendation: Change to MAX(RUN_DATE) or use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY PERIOD_ID ORDER BY RUN_DATE DESC).

redundancies.title: EMPLOYEES.EMPLOYMENT_STATUS and ACTIVE_FLAG encode the same termination state
redundancies.description: An employee with EMPLOYMENT_STATUS='TERMINATED' should always have ACTIVE_FLAG='N'. Conversely, ACTIVE_FLAG='Y' employees should have STATUS other than TERMINATED. PKG_EMPLOYEE.terminate_employee sets both, but there is no CHECK constraint ensuring their consistency. A partial update could produce TERMINATED employees with ACTIVE_FLAG='Y' or ACTIVE employees with ACTIVE_FLAG='N'.
redundancies.divergence_risk: LOW-MEDIUM — queries filtering on one but not both could return incorrect results
redundancies.recommendation: Add a CHECK constraint or trigger ensuring EMPLOYMENT_STATUS='TERMINATED' ↔ ACTIVE_FLAG='N'. Or remove ACTIVE_FLAG from EMPLOYEES since EMPLOYMENT_STATUS provides a richer status.

redundancies.title: PAYROLL_RUNS.APPROVED_BY stores VARCHAR2 username while SALARY_RECORDS.APPROVED_BY stores NUMBER(EMP_ID)
redundancies.description: Two 'approved by' columns use different data types and semantics. SALARY_RECORDS stores EMP_ID (numeric FK-ish); PAYROLL_RUNS stores username string. Inconsistent — makes auditing approval authority harder. Neither is formally FKed to EMPLOYEES.
redundancies.divergence_risk: LOW — inconsistency only; no functional bug
redundancies.recommendation: Standardize: store EMP_ID in both columns. Add soft FK documentation.

redundancies.title: DEPT_ID=30 manager set twice in seed data with different values
redundancies.description: The seed script updates the manager of department 30 twice, with the second update (EMP_ID=30, Rachel Thompson) overwriting the first (EMP_ID=3, Michael OConnor). The first UPDATE is dead code — the end state is EMP_ID=30 as manager. Intent is ambiguous.
redundancies.divergence_risk: LOW — seed data only; no runtime impact
redundancies.recommendation: Remove the first UPDATE; keep only the intended final value.
